quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what rule must you follow?

options.text: You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You may go 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass only in a passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass only in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must happen only where it is safe and legal. You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in designated passing zones.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to handle first.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding without a headlight.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, stay alert and ready to respond. Spot hazards early and decide what to do first. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep enough space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle mirrors?
questions.correctAnswerText: Often
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. This helps you see hazards behind you.

questions.question: What material should you look for in a protective jacket or pants?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets, no matter how fast they are going.

questions.question: At what point does alcohol start to impair your riding ability?

options.text: Once you reach the legal limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit
questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment starts well below the legal limit.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up or brake, as both make wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Both take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars stop in about the same distance. However, wet or slippery roads make it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: How many drinks can you have before alcohol affects your riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking alcohol. It is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle rider adjust their space cushion?

options.text: Keep it the same at all times.
Change it based on road and traffic conditions.
Do not use a space cushion in most situations.
Avoid space cushions to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change it based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Increase your space cushion when stopping takes longer than usual. Give yourself more distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Decrease how far behind other vehicles you stay.
Increase how far behind other vehicles you stay.
Avoid using your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase how far behind other vehicles you stay.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distance in the dark than in daylight. Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles when riding at night. Use your high beam whenever you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface ahead, you should:

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle leans to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid riding over an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it as close to a 90-degree angle as possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat so your knees can absorb some of the impact. Just before hitting the obstacle, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway from a ramp on your right may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left side of your lane so they can share it if needed.
Move into another lane if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane if needed.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles merging onto the highway from an entrance ramp. Change to a lane farther from the ramp if necessary. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give the vehicle room to safely enter the highway.

questions.question: If you are riding directly next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside until the next exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if danger appears. If you find yourself next to another vehicle, either speed up or drop back.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, such as speed limits, are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Shoes that do not cover the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: For protection while riding, wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Shoes should have low heels so they do not catch on foot pegs or rough surfaces. Leather gloves or gloves made of other tough materials protect your hands in a crash and help you grip the controls better.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat (if you are sure which one that is).

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: In a group, less experienced riders should ride toward the front, just behind the leader. This way experienced riders can easily watch them.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and brightly-colored clothing whenever you ride a motorcycle. Crashes happen during the day and at night. Wear visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: How should you secure a load in a sidecar?

options.text: Allow the load to move freely.
Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure all loads in a sidecar so the weight does not shift. This keeps the motorcycle balanced. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you are slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you are slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: How should you brake on a slippery surface?

options.text: Apply the brakes more quickly than usual.
Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
Do not use the rear brake.
Do not use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes more gently than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, apply the brakes gently and with caution when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a flat tire. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is a better sign of tire failure.
